en: During a typhoon, stay indoors because strong winds can turn loose objects like unsecured metal sheets into dangerous flying projectiles.
Always boil floodwater or tap water for at least one minute before drinking to kill harmful bacteria like cholera.
If the ocean water suddenly recedes during an earthquake, immediately run to higher ground because a deadly tsunami is approaching.
Always wash your hands with soap after playing in soil to prevent hookworm larvae from entering your bare skin.
Never look directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses, because its intense ultraviolet rays can permanently damage your eyes.
Never taste unknown rocks or minerals during field trips because some, like cinnabar, contain highly toxic mercury.
When observing the solar system, never look directly at the sun without certified eclipse glasses to prevent permanent eye damage.
The moon's gravitational pull creates high tides that can hide underwater drop-offs and create dangerous rip currents for swimmers.
During an earthquake, drop to the ground, cover your head under a sturdy desk, and hold on until shaking stops.
Drink plenty of water during hot weather because high humidity prevents sweat from evaporating, increasing your risk of heatstroke.
During a thunderstorm, stay inside a fully enclosed metal vehicle or building because lightning can fatally strike you outdoors.
Wear an N95 mask during a volcanic ashfall to prevent fine, abrasive rock particles from damaging your lungs.
